name: Green (Crayola)
lede: Green (Crayola) is the shade of green sold under Crayola's plain "Green" crayon, a cooler, more teal-leaning green than the word green alone suggests.

sections.title: The crayon box's own green
sections.body:
Our library files this swatch as the color behind Crayola's crayon simply named "Green", distinct from the general color word [[green]] it is paired with [1]. The qualifier "(Crayola)" marks it as one of several named variants of [[green]] in our data, alongside entries such as [[green-pigment|Green (Pigment)]] [1].

It sits close to a cluster of near-duplicate names: [[jade|Jade]] and [[green-crayola|Dark Seafoam]] are both almost the same color, [[vivid-green|Vivid Green]] is a shade duller, and [[jade-green|Jade Green]] is more vivid [2]. A separate entry in the color-standard system, Green (Munsell), lands only 1.5 units away, which means two institutions each assign their own "Green" to almost the same point on screen [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries a color close enough to this one over enough of its canvas to count, as photographed [3]. Crayola's own pigment mixes were designed for wax crayons on paper under indoor light, not for painters' palettes, so the absence is expected rather than surprising [3].
